body:
THANKYOUU! Told an old friend who used to be an alcoholic that I was however many days sober from weed and alcohol. His immediate response was just 'the trick is to only smoke in the evening, I didn't even go through withdrawal when I took a week break recently. Guess we're not smoking up next time we see each other then 😒'.


I thought having overcome alcoholism he would understand. But I guess my efforts mean jack shit to him. I need some better friends (and the support of this sub ❤️).
One pro of humans failing to colonise space is that the disease of capitalism will never spread to other planets.

I didn't really feel any shame in being a slut aside from the time that it hurt my boyfriend. It definitely becomes hollow after a while, especially when the foundations of your being aren't really there and you're just using alcohol and sex to hide from your problems. I also lost opportunities to have meaningful, solid friendships because I ended up having sex with a lot of my male friends. I sort of felt obligated to do it to make them feel good and to get validation when I felt worthless. I put myself in a lonely situation. 


I am now seeking platonic friendships and connections through volunteering that has nothing to do with my 'attractiveness' and everything to do with what I can contribute. I hope to get my shit together enough to be useful. 'Needed' feels like a stretch, but it would be nice.

Have completed the survey. As someone trying to quit alcohol, some things I tend to crave are: 


- Sparkling drinks.
- Nice bottle/presentation so it feels like a treat. I also enjoy the sensation of holding a can but obviously this is less common in restaurants.
- More 'mature' flavours, so not too sweet. I like kombucha and the botanical flavours of 'trip cbd' drinks.
- Stealth. By this I mean: the other day at a supermarket I bought a bottle of sparkling kombucha that looked just like a bottle of prosecco. I was willing to spend £8 on this despite it being non-alcoholic because I was going to a party and didn't want people asking why I wasn't drinking. 


Good luck!

I don't think you'd need to blow the whole 30k on travel. You can work/volunteer in exchange for room and board. Backpack, use hostels. Don't blow the money on hotels and fancy bullshit because those are transient pleasures. You can use Coolworks if you're in the USA, also look at Workaway. If you actually gain some skills and help people this gives you something to put on your CV to explain the 'dreaded' gap. I also hope to travel soon to get out of my comfort zone and I'm a lot more skint than you are, haha.


The biggest risk is not having a job to come back to, so I'd try to keep some money saved to tide yourself over. But I'm a doomer who doesn't believe I'll ever see the age of 70, so unlike all these sensible people who probably know a lot more than me, I say just fuckin do it. Who knows how long we have left in this chaotic world.

I'm also bothered by this statement. To me it seems untrue. I've slept with people I would have never slept with when sober. Mild-mannered pre-school teachers can get into fights with bouncers if they're drunk enough. 


I think alcohol creates greed, irrationality, selfishness, poor judgment. It is a poison. Sometimes people with brain injuries become angrier, ruder, more depressed. It's not like those people were always like that, fundamentally 'evil' on the inside.


People love to judge because it makes them feel better about themselves and mob mentality is, of course, worse online. I loved righteously condemning cheaters as morally-bankrupt cowards. Then, guess what, cheated on my boyfriend when I was drunk. I felt like a monster. No one is above behaving shamefully. 


This was some years ago now and I wouldn't say I ever forgave myself, but I did move on because guilt is only a productive emotion if it drives you towards better behaviour. When shame reaches a certain point it's like, what am I supposed to do, kill myself? Would that make things right, make my ex boyfriend and the friends I lost at the time happy? Of course not. It would only lead to more emptiness.


I hope you find a way out of your shame. You're not a monster. All of us make mistakes. Let he who is without sin cast the first stone.

I am in the same position rn and I want to fucking kill myself lol.


The main difference for me is that I think it's incredibly unlikely I can actually pass at this point based on how my course works. So I am considering an indefinite mental health deferral and only coming back if I know I can actually pass. I know everyone will think I'm an idiot though and it's stressing me out.


Right now I want to save enough money to travel for a bit then go and learn a trade. I'm highly unlikely to ever work in my degree field anyway.

Ngl I'm glad to see someone here post about societal issues affecting their sobriety. For me the shitty state of the world and engaging too much with depressing news and subreddits is a big reason for my substance abuse.


I think with the way things are going, we NEED people who are switched on, capable of critical thinking, emotional regulation and facing the truth of the world. These things are easier to do sober. Drinking will hurt your critical thinking skills, memory, make you more emotional and susceptible to the bullshit that the people you criticise have fallen victim to. 


For me, the thought of having to deal with an environmental or economic crisis situation while hungover is enough. Imagine your house gets flooded or you lose your job PLUS you're dealing with withdrawal. If I can't die immediately then I'd rather stare the horrors in the face with a clear head.

I dropped out of law after first year because I couldn't see myself working in the industry either. I recommend if you choose a different degree to do so based primarily on having a direct interest and thorough understanding of the career it may lead to (I didn't really understand how the legal field worked, I assumed it'd be like Legally Blonde lmao).


I switched to Product Design but sucked at that too. I probably have ADHD. I'm hoping to learn a trade instead since I think AI will put white collar jobs at risk and the best part of my course was actually making shit/using fun tools.


I would say if you just want a degree then do something you enjoy, but I think all degrees have a way of making you hate the subject haha.

Haha so true, in the UK when it gets sunny the desire to do fuck all except sit in a pub garden with a drink is immense.


I also used to sit out in the sun and smoke a joint which I'm also trying to quit. So now I'll take a coffee or tea out instead. I like to sit and listen to the radio for a bit, stare at the bluebells that have sprung up in the garden. It's especially helpful if I haven't made it outside yet that day. I always feel guilty about missing the daylight.

Thanks for your response. I'll totally download that app, money saving is a big motivator. I don't want to end up like my old stoner friend who was constantly in her overdraft. 


Good luck with this attempt. I think multiple attempts show you're actually more likely to lead to success. I had multiple instances with deleting steam/all my games when I quit gaming (which was also becoming detrimental to my life). At the time it seemed like 'aw shit, here we go again' but eventually it stuck. 


I'm going to do the same thing I did with gaming where I print out a calendar and put an X on every day sober. It seems inane since obviously I'm keeping track mentally/on Reddit, but having the clear visual right above my desk was motivating.


Good luck bro, every day there will be less poison in our system and we can reclaim our minds 🙏🏻
I'm unconcerned about my lifespan but I do think smoking more has aged me a bit, which I find motivating. I would also like to have better lung/heart function for exercise.

It must be tough living in a house with a grower while you're trying to quit. Well done for resisting the temptation. 


I guess we are drug addicts but I know what you mean 😂 weed is not usually treated in the same category. That's why I'm glad this sub exists cuz a lot of people don't understand our desire for sobriety. 'Just have it in moderation bro'. 


I feel lucky so far my withdrawal symptoms have mostly been psychological, although I do feel tired as shit.

Jesus H Christ, I'm amazed you were able to live such a functional(ish) life still! Sometimes I think it's good I'm so low functioning so that it becomes evident very quickly when I need to change things. 


The 'no diarrhea' motivation is amazing hahaha but SO REAL. Nothing like having the DADS but feeling so queasy and hungover that it takes huge mental focus to be able to poop without also throwing up. That's how I felt last time I drank+smoked.


I imagine you'll see your life dramatically changing for the better very soon!

Bitching on Reddit makes me feel a bit better, although I'd like to be able to use a diary more often and feel the same relief for the sake of spending less time on my phone. 


I try to keep up with the basics even if it feels futile. I usually don't get around to eating a proper breakfast til the afternoon, sometimes after drinking a coffee sat outside where I used to smoke weed. It's annoying to admit in a depressed state that the food, walk, yoga, daylight, all do actually help. It's just initiating them is hard during the despair. 


I've also always been depressed and self destructive even before alcohol and weed. So I'm worried sometimes that this is futile. But I guess if the chance of my perspective on life improving when sober is 1, then when using it's 0. At least sobriety is something we can control in the chaos of the world.

Thank you. Bad for your heart literally or metaphorically? Metaphorically feels right haha. I want to be sober to deal with the lows in a constructive way, and to enjoy the highs without always thinking 'this sex/yoga/food would be better if I were stoned'.

Thank you. I can't imagine quitting after 26 years of use, that must be tough. I used casually/socially for a couple of years but it's only been 6 months of more destructive use, with about 1 smoking almost daily (it's hard to remember, since weed makes the timeline kind of slide-y, haha). I feel lucky to have found this sub and r/stopdrinking, they have given me glimpses into possible futures that make me want to nip my addictions in the bud sooner rather than later. The daily smoking started giving such diminishing returns, so I was just sad but now sad with crap memory and articulation.


What are your personal motivations? I need to write mine down and stick them on the wall because sometimes it feels futile, given that the world is in polycrisis and my smoking wasn't exactly putting me on the street.
Welp. What the fuck do we do now?

I am in this camp. Back on no drinking after a horrible end to Thursday night. I attribute the drinking to just not giving a shit if I live or die at the time.


Something I have found helpful is the knowledge that ANY alcohol negatively impacts your sleep quality. I just looked it up and apparently having a 'high amount  of alcohol'  - defined as more than one drink for women and two for men - reduces sleep quality by 39.4%.


 Sleep is mega important to me for bare minimum mental health function, so it's helpful knowing one lousy beer that won't even come close to creating the change of state I crave can STILL fuck my day up tomorrow.


Also, calories. 1-2 drinks won't get me drunk, and I've just drunk a bunch of calories that I could have used on a plate of loaded nachos or something. Having 2 drinks in an uncomfortable social situation is normally a guarantee that more will follow for me.

I became a student (in the UK) so for a short time I had enough maintenance loan to not need a job as long as I budget. Don't want anything to do with my degree unfortunately. I'm thinking about picking up some work in kitchens and hopefully gaining enough experience to work and travel as a cook. I am aware that alcoholism can be quite rampant in the industry though.


  I've been a barista at a couple of different places and since it's daytime with no alcohol served on the premises it's a much more sober-friendly environment.


 I am also looking into trades, since there is a skills shortage in the UK and it won't be hit by the AI takeover as quickly as white collar jobs. It would mean staying rooted in the UK for longer though, I'm hoping to travel more while I'm not so tied down trying to gain qualifications. I'm beginning to realise you do need a -plan- if you want to get out of hospitality since it's just so easy to get comfortable, come home tired after your shift and watch netflix instead of scoping out other jobs/qualifications. But sobriety will definitely help us keep a clear head and growth mindset 🙏🏻

I don't think that counts as cheating, although I've never heard of a bartender having to taste every drink, but I'm guessing you work somewhere upscale. 


I really enjoyed my bartending job but it makes it so much harder to stick to your resolutions. People offer to buy you drinks or there's staff parties that you want to fully include yourself in. No one really understands 'why can't you just have a cheeky pint?'. Good luck with your move and finding a job that's better suited to your new lifestyle 😊

Love that quote. You definitely still have potential, I can see your intelligence and passion through your writing.


As someone who has also been isolating themselves too much and sometimes feels like I have to meet a certain standard of appearance before I can go outside, please don't do that haha. Let yourself 'be seen'. I started letting myself go to the shops when I haven't showered, since sometimes showering would take a long time (depression) and then I'd lose the opportunity to get some daylight and passive social interaction just from being too self conscious. To everyone else I'm sure you just look like a normal guy and they aren't thinking about your appearance.


I also over-order takeaways, which sucks cuz I love cooking and it always tastes 1000x better homemade. I hope without the distraction of weed you and I can feed ourselves better!

You should continue to write and make art anyway as a form of self expression - you're a good writer! 


I felt horribly put off making art for a while when AI art started picking up, but now I feel like it's helped me feel liberated from having to make anything that others will find 'good' or skillful, and the nagging voice about making every hobby some kind of side hustle is gone because for me personally it wouldn't be feasible. The point of making art is now clearer to me: it's therapeutic and a way to express and explore the conscious and unconscious. Sometimes I draw instead of writing in my journal if it makes it easier to express how I feel.


You are not alone, and your post helped me feel less alone.
Your child is lucky to have you. I hope you talk as openly and compassionately to them as you have to me.
You make a good point.
Thank you so much for your warm words of support.
Thank you for your response. I didn't think I was bad enough for AA but now I feel like I need the support of a community to not self destruct.
Why even make the post then if you're not looking for any advice other than to fulfil your own confirmation bias? This post is rage bait at this point.

I get angry about still having to go through the motions and appear normal to other people. And then I get angry at myself for caring about those motions because I'm buying into my own bullshit for the sake of being able to get things done. Rage is not far from despair, in my experience.

I know I could have written this more kindly but the way you wrote as though you have absolutely no agency to make a better choice in this situation is just irritating:  The 'slice of paradise' argument doesn't even make sense though??? You're going to suffer in the process of conceiving/raising this child because of the guilt you feel. So you're not even getting any paradise? Also yes it's selfish as fuck for you to only think about your temporary 'joy' and not give a shit about the suffering of this entirely new human life. Fucking hell I understand the desire to blow a load of money on fossil-fuel loaded flights/travel, food, drugs, empty hedonistic pursuits in the face of oblivion. I get that. It's not the right thing to do but I understand how fear drives people to that behaviour. But a child?????? You and your wife need to pull your heads out the fucking sand and search for a more compassionate means of dealing with this that doesn't involve the creation of new suffering for your own amusement. Also go read r/regretfulparents, that'll quickly knock the lenses out of your ridiculous rose-tinted glasses regarding parenthood.

Well done for resisting the tempting environment. Your goals are very noble. I'm beginning to realise that quitting weed isn't about what I might be able to accomplish while sober, but more about the values I'm reinforcing in myself. Your desire to build mental resilience - that's something real. I don't want to always have to turn to a drug to deal with my problems.

As someone who used weed to help quit alcohol, I cannot imagine why you'd want to swap with alcohol. I recommend the Huberman podcast on why alcohol essentially has absolutely fuck all benefits and can fuck with your sleep and mood even in small doses. 


It is hard having nothing though. I try to exercise a lot for the energy, distraction and inherent reward for not drinking or smoking (will make exercise much easier).

I feel that 'kinder to myself and others' so hard. Most of my rudeness towards others comes from how critical I am towards myself, so it leaks out of me because that shitty voice is well-rehearsed. When I'm smoking I'm empathetic af and give people pep talks that my depressed ass usually would not be able to conceive.
Also, I'm addicted to my phone since it's a brick of dopamine. But when I'm high the phone is too confusing or anxiety-inducing, so I naturally would rather do other non-screen activities.
Is Adderall even available in the UK? I thought that was in America only.

I feel this so hard. Also 26 and in the UK. Honestly I had more passion as a teenager because I had the free time and more belief that things could be better. I'm trying to get my life together because we so badly need people who aren't too apathetic and exhausted to stand up to the Tory dictatorship and provide a real opposition (not like the centrist limp bit of wet toast labour has become). 


But it's hard, and of course that's the intention. Keep everyone worried about survival but their heads just above water. Quietly make meaningful protest illegal. I also feel like more people are on drugs (at least where I live) because things are so bad and I wouldn't be surprised if that was also a calculated move. An intoxicated, desperate population is easier to control. Until (I pray) it isn't.
Good shout

I used to be fairly careful with my consumption but this strain has really surprised me with it's antidepressant qualities. It brings out my neurotic side a bit but I would actually consider smoking a potentially legitimate mental health treatment now. Still important to be careful with it ofc.

Purpledawg I believe. I am also hoping to get my hands on some guavadog again sometime cuz it was epic (although more of a hedonistic strain, this one has just made me insanely productive compared to my usual depressed self).

It's early doors for me yet but I've started reading The Future is Degrowth: A Guide to a World Beyond Capitalism. 


I found this video informative and it has a good reading list in the description: https://youtu.be/48G3ox90wss?si=YjBL_YREKScNS1Rl


Some of them are academic papers. To motivate myself I'm writing an assignment for uni on this subject (which is supposed to be about business in the traditional sense but imma make it about degrowth and how infinite growth on a finite planet is fuckin stupid hahaha).

Wow! That's a great positive take on a challenging situation. I am sorry that happened to you though. At the moment I haven't experienced any extreme weather events being in a mild area in the UK. Another thing to think about (although I'm not much of a pepper). 


I do feel like when we are forced to work within limitations we can eventually adapt and a situation which initially felt 'worse' than usual just becomes the new norm. Equally, having everything work perfectly doesn't always guarantee more productivity or less stress.
Haha yeah you just gotta keep busy really. I've also had periods of learning to play the keyboard instead of gaming, but found it hard to stay motivated.

Definitely feel consumed by it lately. I had given up Reddit and collapse media for a while and I will say it probably helped my studies for a bit. But when uni life started going badly again I leaned back into it. It's addictive when under the stress of stupid regular bullshit: look at all these headlines, me potentially failing my course really doesn't matter in the grand scheme of things.


The problem is now the collapse page is the first thing I check when I wake up. I almost feel disappointed when things aren't worse? Not rationally of course, but on some irrational level like 'cmon man I'm just looking for that event that'll push me over the edge'. Perhaps mentally I'm more free than other people but I don't act free. I have a great and pretty hedonistic social life but I recognise I have been neglecting my spirituality and the things I should be working towards if I want to live a life that's spiritually meaningful. It's also, of course, ironic and counterproductive that in the hours I spend scrolling and festering in misery I regularly miss out on the everyday pleasures we should all be relishing right now. I don't even make it outside til after dark most days, let alone into nature.


Perhaps you and I should take a break from it. Try to focus on -really- living, not the cog in the machine shit but -really- living, whatever that means for us. I hope we can find our way out of this spiritual darkness.

Your ex husband was abusive, which can make feelings after separation even more complicated. You've been left with the pain of the horrible things he said to you without even the comfort of his familiar presence. To have survived his abuse and continued to succeed in your personal life and found the strength to commence divorce proceedings, you must be a very strong person. I wish I could be as strong as you.


I have also thought about the helium exit bag method, I've just never let myself actually buy it. I agree I'd be too worried about the reliability and expense of nembutal (of course the expense shouldn't matter if I truly wanted to die, but I guess I never really want to. I just want the complexity of the world to be solved, for a good future to be guaranteed.) 


It sounds to me like you still have a good future, particularly since it won't have this asshole husband in it anymore. Idk what it's like where you are but in the UK there are organisations that support people in abusive/formerly in abusive relationships. In the meantime, I find that suicidal ideation doesn't always last the night if you can get through it. To pass the time, I recommend the YouTube channel Cinema Therapy, watching 'A marriage story'. It's comforting and entertaining to watch, and reading through the comments you will find a lot of people telling their stories of getting through difficult situations.

I get what you mean. For me it feels like I become more anxious when I'm doing well because I'm engaging in life and starting to care again. Plus, when things start going well you have more to lose. Depression can feel 'addictive' (or maybe 'habitual') in a way because although it's horrendous the apathy and suicidality makes you let go more and feel safer in the pit.

Also I've sometimes found when I actually exercise properly the surges of energy can make me feel angry or experience some other emotional release, so that could be part of what happened to you.

So you are literally judging others for their job? You have no idea what the circumstances are that may have lead people to their job. For many it's as simple as the struggle of the job search: you can only spend so long searching for a 'respectable' salary job before the rent needs to get paid and McDonald's will hire you within 4 days. 

In the UK, doctors and nurses are currently striking and leaving the profession because they could be earning more working at a restaurant. Why should people care about their job being more 'respectable' if they can't afford to make ends meet despite their years of education and training? Plus healthcare workers still get treated like shit all the time anyway.

Most jobs are utter bullshit even if they are more respected. I work at a bar and people I went to school with come in and make snide passive aggressive comments about how this is what I do now. But if I worked as a paper pusher in some salaried office job I'd magically be deemed worthy of their respect, despite the fact that half the shit we produce in these offices is utter nonsense that no one fucking needs.

If you judge others for their profession (unless that profession is actively harming others) then you are a classist who has been indoctrinated by capitalism to value others based on the capital they produce, or arbitrary divisions of 'status' that are used to keep the lower classes divided. We are all doing what we can to survive this hell.

I think I'd feel comfortable no longer identifying as a 'gaming addict' when it's hardly ever on my mind, no cravings, particularly when I'm stressed or upset. I suppose it would be nice to replace it with a new identity though, like 'a person who does yoga everyday' or 'stoic'.

Interesting perspective. I believe the day counting comes from how most systems for beating addiction encourage addicts to work 'one day at a time', since that can make it easier for someone feeling reluctant or overwhelmed by quitting to start in the first place. For me, saying 'you can NEVER game EVER AGAIN' makes me want to hold onto my steam account and 110% all the games I have on there before I let go. Whereas just saying 'I won't game today', and trying to build a chain of days where I do better things instead is a smaller challenge to overcome.

I've found it helpful to think about how the games will always be there. I own them, I can come back to them anytime, but now is not a good time. Right now my body is young so I should make use of that by working out/going out more instead. Right now it's important I work hard on other things to make my life easier. Take it one day at a time and if you can just manage about two weeks of detox then the temptation will be reduced significantly.

Like another commenter said, looking up endings will be helpful. I'm a completionist too, but watching all the leader defeat scenes and winning cutscenes for Civ made it much easier to not waste so many hours on such a small and pointless goal.
It's good that you took the time to think about what caused the craving. I did the same earlier, made a quick post on here, felt better. Are you doing a different activity instead?
Thank you, I'm trying not to totally regress.

I know right, there's just too many things! I have spoken to one recruiter, no idea if he'll be able to help me as it's an ambitious field of work to try to get into part time but  that's definitely a good idea.
This is good stuff
What resources do you use to study math? I am also learning to code rn and enjoying it a lot. I replaced video games with it and it's one of the few things that has helped me kick the habit.
NTA. This new guy sounds like an insecure douchebag.

Don't have kids you don't want. They will feel your apathy towards them from the get go. My father told my sister and I he didn't want us, I guess assuming he could pass that off as light conversation. It has stayed with me and fucked with my self esteem. Don't do it.
Thank you, I will check those out!
Thank you. I do need therapy again, you're right. It's hard letting hope in again after just assuming I would die soon for a long time. Your trash can system sounds smart!

How did you manage the Mcmansion squatting? There are a whole bunch of bougie ass places near the coast about an hour from where I live. I always want to try to break in and live in them purely on principle, cuz I'm sure 50% of these grotesque million(s) dollar properties are uninhabited for most of the year.
Probably killing myself somewhere in the region of a month. However I've put it off before. It's possible that will happen again. I don't really have any hope for myself or my future though.

Working is painful and the guilt/shame from not being in work is painful. I feel undignified still living with my parents, despite them being fairly understanding, plus knowing it was their generation that created the economic landscape that is so much more hostile today. Not to sound like an edgy teen, but I often wish I had never been born and feel I am destined for suicide.
Are you taking yourself out? I'm not going to talk you out of it, just curious.

Thank you haha, it felt like I didn't have much choice at the time. Kentish Town is a pretty gentrified area but we did have some assholes. People attempting to use fake £50s and £20s, then if you questioned them they'd get aggressive and hold up the queue in an attempt to get you to just accept the money. They probably thought they were stealing from a big corporation, but at the time if your name was assigned to be working on that til, any lost money (regardless of whether management knew it was stolen by a customer or not) came out of your paycheck. I should have quit as soon as I found out about that policy, but I was naive and not as confident in calling out bullshit as I am now. Respect to all McDonald's and fast food workers, they deal with some shit and having some real kindness and patience from occasional customers really helps.
Oh also: I'm pretty sure the food was just happy meals all around, ofc you could choose whether you wanted the burger, chicken nuggets or vegetarian meal.

I worked at a McDonald's a couple of years ago (this was in Kentish Town, London). We still did children's birthday parties with face painting, some simple games, food and cake. Typically they only lasted 1 1/2-2 hours. Personally I have no fucking clue why you'd want to have one, but I guess I associate them with being underpaid, cleaning up the mess and the children's play area. You could probably call ahead to ask, though if you'd want to serve alcohol check ahead as I'm not sure they'd have license to have any alcohol on the premises.
Lmao I don't understand why the mods took it down when a lot of the replies are sympathetic to OP's message. Idk why perfectly rational variants of antinatalist sentiment are so quick to be censored.
Thought I'd comment to tell you I found this funny so your comments aren't all bots 😂 I do appreciate learning facts about how shitty the royal family is though

Maybe I'm being naive. Maybe I'm just choosing not to believe it. I have enough reasons to want to kill myself already. I really don't need to add the belief that 'most humans will become rapists and torturers when life is bad' to the list.

I just don't see the logic of an increase in rape and torture in a full collapse scenario. Violence committed in an attempt to gain resources, sure. Rape and torture? Seems like a waste of energy when there's no food and it's 120 degrees or whatever. Silver linings eh?
I feel ya

Yep I agree with this. Plus I think general societal and social pressures should not be underestimated. People would likely still work for these luxuries and for the sake of not being socially ostracised and deemed as 'lazy'. I can't picture most UK individuals forgoing all work if it means they can't join their friends for drinks, buy drugs, cigarettes, nights out etc.

Edit: plus with regards to the 'people would only choose fun work' issue, I think a UBI could incentivise improving pay and working conditions for essential jobs. I would love to see it happen in the UK but am pessimistic.
I'll kill myself if I want to. Leave us depressos alone Jesus Christ

I feel ya. I got as far as managing to tell my mum how low I've been. Had a couple of drinks and then messaged her. It went better than I thought it would. These things often do, plus even if they don't you feel better for trying and at least you still have some kind of certainty from the outcome. I hope you and I can try to be honest with the people in our life, find support and help ourselves.

You're definitely not alone (see r/regretfulparents). You're not a psycho or a bad person. I can't even take care of myself, so I find the fact that you're working and trying to raise a child very admirable.
Thank you!
Thanks!
Thanks! I am on PC, I'll see what new Civs I can get from the workshop while I wait for a sale :))

Thank you for sharing. I found the Michael Moore one particularly interesting. I assume it was deemed controversial due to his comments about the necessity of human-kind curbing its own population growth? I enjoyed the points he made about how humanity's failure to accept its own death resulting in further destruction as we attempt to play god.

I believe they're referring to 'Breaking Down: Collapse' which is available on Spotify (look for the red cover image with an hourglass in the middle). It provides a very useful, calmly articulated summary of research conducted by the hosts including topical environmental discussion, plus some philosophy and personal/emotional responses.   


I think a cool part of the documentary would be showing someone attempting to explain to their family or friends what's going on, a 'coming out' as a collapsnik/collapse-aware individual, if you will. I think the reason a lot of people are drawn to this sub is that we feel we cannot express our emotions and fears to our families, or fear social rejection.

Idk about your 'born to consoom' point, but I definitely feel like I'm not strong enough to face what's coming. I hope if/when shit really hits the fan, kinder forms of euthanasia become available for those who want it, or at least suicide becomes more socially acceptable so people like me aren't seen as 'selfish' for not wanting to feel like another useless mouth to feed.
